products.name: Logseq AI
products.note: Open-source knowledge base; local-first; graph database; privacy-focused

reading.body:
Logseq is a privacy-first, open-source knowledge base that runs locally on users' devices rather than centralizing data on external servers, positioning it distinctly against cloud-dependent note-taking tools.

The local-first architecture matters for AI because it keeps training data and user content off shared infrastructure. This reduces both the compute footprint required to run the service and the networking demands that would otherwise route user queries through centralized systems. For a knowledge management tool, staying local means the cost of scale does not compound through backend server multiplication.

The graph database structure organizes notes as interconnected nodes rather than flat documents, which has implications for how any integrated AI features can traverse and reason over user knowledge. This structure is computationally different from sequential storage and affects what kind of inference workloads the product can reasonably support on consumer hardware.

The data does not cover Logseq's actual usage volume, infrastructure spending, or whether Logseq AI features run on-device or route to external compute. It does not show whether the company operates its own data centers, leases cloud capacity, or relies entirely on user machines for computation. Without those details, the local-first design tells us architectural intent, not actual power or building consumption.

profile_text.body:
Logseq describes itself as a privacy-first, open-source platform for knowledge management and collaboration. The company's core product is a local-first knowledge base that stores data on the user's own device rather than on external servers, and it uses a graph database structure to organize notes and information.

The site tracks one AI-related product, Logseq AI, categorized under notes, knowledge, and meetings, and characterized as open-source, local-first, graph-database-driven, and privacy-focused. No litigation, MCP servers, SEC filings, or patent records are held for the company.
